name: Tuna & cheese patties (קציצות טונה וגבינה)

source.author: Hebrew recipe (screenshot)
source.notes: Analyzed from a pasted Hebrew ingredient list. Method not shown (assumed mixed and baked/pan-fried patties; no cooking oil listed, so baked assumed — add ~120 kcal/tbsp if fried). The tuna line ('Steakist*') had a footnote that was cut off. Tuna drained weight (~280 g for 2 cans), Shkedi soft-cheese values, and servings are estimated.

steps: Mix drained tuna, cottage cheese, Shkedi cheese, beaten eggs, breadcrumbs, grated/chopped onion, grated yellow cheese, salt and pepper.
Form patties and bake (or pan-fry) until set and golden. (Method not shown — baked assumed.)

him.verdict: A strong high-protein dish — 29 g protein for ~283 kcal (~10 g protein per 100 kcal) from tuna + eggs + a stack of cheeses, with good selenium (~45 mcg, a sperm micro from the tuna/eggs), calcium, and a little omega-3. Fat (~12 g) and sodium (~400 mg) come mostly from the yellow cheese + cottage/Shkedi; you can lighten by trimming the yellow cheese. Canned light tuna is fine for you in these modest per-serving amounts (~⅓ can/serving).
flags: fat/sodium from the cheeses (yellow cheese is the lever)
no cooking oil listed — bake to keep it lean
suggested_mods: Bake rather than fry to keep fat down (no oil was listed anyway)
Drop or halve the 100 g yellow cheese — biggest fat/sodium lever with little protein loss
Serve over salad/greens to add the fiber + micros the dish is light on

her_preconception.verdict: Nutrient-rich for her — protein, calcium, choline (eggs), selenium, iodine, some omega-3 — BUT this is the one dish carrying a real mercury flag: it's tuna. That keeps it a 'fine in moderation, mind the details' rather than a staple. The per-serving tuna load is modest (~⅓ can), which helps.
prenatal_highlights: some omega-3 EPA/DHA from the tuna
modest per-serving tuna amount (~⅓ can) keeps mercury exposure lower

safety_advisories.note: TUNA = mercury. Use LIGHT/skipjack canned tuna, not albacore/white or high-mercury species — 'Steakist' steak-style may be a larger (higher-mercury) species, so check. Once actively trying/pregnant, keep total tuna to ~2 servings/week of light tuna (1/week if albacore).
safety_advisories.swap: light/skipjack tuna, or swap to canned salmon/sardines (lower mercury, more omega-3)

safety_advisories.note: Cheeses must be pasteurized (Israeli cottage/yellow/Shkedi are) — fine. Bake eggs fully.

suggested_mods: Swapping the tuna for canned SALMON removes the mercury flag AND raises omega-3 + vitamin D — a strictly better preconception version
Confirm the tuna is light/skipjack and count it toward her weekly tuna limit in lihitrack
